Article Title: Forces fortify key Arunachal bridge to fight dam objectors
Article Text:

DITE DIME: Anti-dam protests have prompted a major security build-up at the Dite-Dime bridge in Arunachal Pradesh, a key crossing towards the India-China border that connects four proposed drilling sites for a pre-feasibility survey of the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.Forces have heavily fortified the bridge, deploying large numbers of CAPF personnel, as it has become a focal point of the anti-dam movement, hosting dharnas and protests against the proposed survey. Officials said 30 companies of CAPF had been deployed across protest-hit districts. Three companies of Assam Police Battalion were stationed in Pasighat.Also known as 65 Bridge, the Dite-Dime bridge is a critical bottleneck on the Dite-Dime-Migging highway towards Tuting near the Line of Actual Control. At least four women were wounded in a clash at Dite-Dime on Oct 23 during a 12-hour bandh. More than 150 supporters allegedly threw stones at security personnel, tried to breach barricades and damaged security vehicles, police sources said.
Article Summary: Anti-dam protests have prompted a major security build-up at the Dite-Dime bridge in Arunachal Pradesh. The bridge is a key crossing towards the India- China border. It connects four proposed drilling sites for a pre-feasibility survey of the 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project.

Article Title: Oil prices slip as peace hopes ease supply fears, Middle East tensions limit losses
Article Text:
Crude prices relax

Houthi attacks keep supply concerns alive

Conflicting signals from US-Iran peace efforts

Oil prices declined on Thursday as traders weighed the possibility of fresh diplomatic developments between the US and Iran against the risk of further supply disruptions from escalating attacks in the Middle East.Brent crude fell by $0.85, or 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%, to $101.90. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%.The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to restart peace negotiations, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.The possibility of further negotiations has offered some relief to oil markets, but the threat of an intensification in regional hostilities continues to weigh on the outlook for supplies. Concerns include renewed attacks by Yemen's Houthis and the possibility that the US could launch an attack on Iran after its mid-term elections on November 3.Fresh developments in the conflict involving the Houthis and Saudi Arabia added to uncertainty on Thursday.The Saudi-led coalition fighting the group said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's eastern region early in the day, with hostilities between the two sides showing no signs of easing.The latest incident followed an attack on Aden airport on Wednesday, according to Yemeni government forces. A day earlier, the Houthis had said they struck Saudi Arabia's largest oil refinery with a missile, escalating their attacks against the world's second-largest crude producer after the United States.Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the reported strike on the refinery, which has a capacity of 550,000 barrels per day.The continuing attacks have kept concerns over potential supply disruptions in focus even as diplomatic efforts offer the possibility of easing tensions.Efforts to find a way to end the war involving the US, Israel and Iran have produced mixed signals. An official briefed on the negotiations said Qatari mediators had presented Iran with a new draft agreement to end the conflict.However, a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals, describing them as unacceptable ideas that did not constitute an offer.Iran's foreign minister said on Wednesday that Tehran was continuing to give diplomacy a chance to succeed. The minister also flagged the possibility of completing Iran's seven-day plan in less than a week if it was adopted.The contrasting positions leave the prospects for a diplomatic resolution uncertain, while the possibility of renewed negotiations has contributed to the downward movement in crude prices.Meanwhile, US inventory data provided another factor for oil markets to follow. The US Energy Information Administration said that energy companies had withdrawn 1.9 million barrels of crude oil from storage during the week ended October 23.Gasoline inventories, however, increased by 3.9 million barrels, against analysts' expectations of a decline of 900,000 barrels.The opposing movements in crude and gasoline stockpiles added to the mixed signals facing oil markets as traders assessed the impact of diplomatic developments, regional attacks and US inventory data on prices.
Article Summary: Brent crude fell by 0.74%, to $114.50 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) dropped $0.91, or 0.89%. The decline pared gains made in the previous session, when Brent advanced 1.3% and WTI climbed 3%. The prospect of a diplomatic breakthrough emerged after US vice president JD Vance sent a letter to Iranian security council chief Mohsen Rezaei.

MK Stalin tears into Vijay government over searches linked to KN Nehru

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister and DMK president M K Stalin on Thursday accused the C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of using vigilance raids as political theatre ahead of the Tiruchirappalli East by-election. Stalin also asserted that the searches would not intimidate DMK workers.The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Thursday conducted searches at 25 locations across Tamil Nadu linked to former minister and DMK leader K N Nehru in connection with an alleged Rs 634-crore cash-for-jobs scam involving recruitment in the Municipal Administration and Water Supply (MAWS) department.In a post on X, Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)chief Stalin described the action as “Vettri Vendetta Politics” and accused the state government of attempting to divert attention from law-and-order concerns.“The Chief Minister, who has turned Tamil Nadu into a state where women, children, and the elderly are no longer safe, is now contemplating whether to conduct a 'Roadshow' or a 'Raidshow' to divert the attention of the people and the media's 'Breaking News',” Stalin said.The DMK chief also accused the ruling party of selectively targeting former ministers while inducting leaders facing corruption allegations.“TVK, a 'TN Branch Washing Machine' that is turning all the corrupt vermin into 'bargaining horses' and inducting them into its party, is pursuing a plan of 'Vettri Vendetta Politics' by targeting only the former ministers of the DMK regime.As always, this will fail before the law and hang its head in shame before the public!” he said.Linking the searches to the upcoming by-election, Stalin alleged that the operation was intended to generate social media content and provide Vijay with political talking points.“These raids, conducted to produce 'Reels' for the Tiruchirappalli East by-election and to allow the Chief Minister to scream on stage in various modulations under the guise of 'punch dialogues,' will not make even the toenail of the lowermost DMK cadre tremble!” he said.The DVAC searches follow the registration of a case against Nehru and others after the Madras High Court directed a probe into alleged irregularities flagged by the Enforcement Directorate (ED). The allegations concern bribes collected from candidates in exchange for government postings during Nehru’s tenure as minister.The agency is examining documents and financial records to trace the suspected money trail and establish evidence relating to the recruitment process.Nehru has also moved the Supreme Court through a special leave petition challenging the Madras High Court’s October 26 order dismissing his review petition against the registration of the first information report (FIR).Stalin further criticised the government over rising prices and governance, saying, “The entire nation, not just Tamil Nadu, is mocking this TVK government, which is plaguing the people with lawlessness, a rusted administration, and scorching price hikes.”
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister M K Stalin accused the C Joseph Vijay-led Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of using vigilance raids as political theatre. The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) on Thursday conducted searches at 25 locations across Tamil Nadu linked to former minister K N Nehru.

Article Title: 'Battle scars': Massive stitches on Captain Smit Machchhar head draw attention as UAE honours hero Indian pilot
Article Text:
The medals were presented by Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum at a presidential reception

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A massive line of stitches running across the back of Captain Smit Machchhar’s head has brought the severity of the Indian pilot’s injuries into focus as he received a prestigious UAE honour for his role in thwarting the mid-air cockpit attack.Far-right UK leader Tommy Robinson shared a photograph of the scar on social media, praising Machchhar for his bravery. “Not all heroes wear capes. Some wear battle scars. Hero Indian Captain Smit Machchhar. The world salutes you,” Robinson wrote.The Indian captain and his fellow flydubai crew members were conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan in recognition of their efforts to protect passengers during the September 30 incident aboard flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv.The medals were presented by Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum at a presidential reception. The UAE leadership praised the crew for their courage, professionalism and commitment to passenger safety.Machchhar was seriously injured when his co-pilot allegedly attacked him with a crash axe and stabbed him inside the cockpit. The aircraft, carrying more than 170 people, reportedly plunged nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds during the incident.Despite being covered in blood and severely wounded, Machchhar managed to release the cockpit door lock, allowing passengers and crew members to overpower the co-pilot. Two other flydubai pilots who were travelling on board then took control of the aircraft and landed it safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The motive behind the alleged attack remains unclear. The co-pilot, identified by Israeli officials as an Omani national, was taken into custody.Machchhar was initially treated at a hospital in Tabuk before being transferred to Abu Dhabi for further treatment. Sheikh Hamdan had earlier visited him in hospital and praised his courage in helping avert a potential tragedy.The First Class Order of Zayed II is a high-level UAE civil decoration awarded in recognition of distinguished service and exceptional contributions. The honour recognises the crew's actions in protecting the lives of those aboard the aircraft.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was seriously injured when his co-pilot allegedly attacked him with a crash axe and stabbed him inside the cockpit. The Indian captain and his fellow flydubai crew members were conferred the First Class Order of Zayed II by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The UAE leadership praised the crew for their courage, professionalism and commitment to passenger safety.

Article Title: 'They will fly': MEA on direct India-Taiwan flights after Pakistan blocks airspace over 'One-China' policy
Article Text:
MEA's remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday indicated that direct air connectivity between India and Taiwan could be explored, amid reports that Pakistan has barred Taiwanese airlines from using its airspace under its “One China” policy.“My sense is, if there are direct flights then they will fly,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said when asked about the possibility of direct flights between India and Taiwan.The remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace, in a move that highlights Islamabad's support for Beijing's position on Taiwan.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif confirmed the country's position to Bloomberg News, saying its aviation policy permits only mainland Chinese airlines to fly over its airspace.“The aviation division follows the One China policy — only mainland China is allowed,” Asif said.“We have permitted only Chinese airlines to fly over Pakistan,” he added.Pakistan is the first country reported to have taken such a step against Taiwanese carriers. Bloomberg, citing flight-tracking data, reported that China Airlines Ltd and EVA Airways Corp had not flown over Pakistani airspace since the morning of October 25.The restriction came to light after aviation observers noticed that some Taiwanese flights had begun taking longer routes to reach Europe, flying entirely over Russian airspace since the weekend.According to Flightradar24 data, a China Airlines flight from Taipei to Rome on October 24 flew through Russian airspace, bypassing its earlier route through India, Pakistan and Turkmenistan.The move comes as China continues to urge other countries to support its claim that Taiwan is part of its territory. Beijing considers Taiwan a part of China, while Taipei maintains that the island is self-governed and rejects Beijing's claim.Pakistan's decision also underlines its close ties with China, which Islamabad has described as an “iron-clad friendship”. The two countries have maintained an “all-weather” partnership since establishing diplomatic relations in 1951.In January, Pakistan described Taiwan as an “inalienable part” of China and reiterated its commitment to the One China principle.
Article Summary: “My sense is, if there are direct flights then they will fly,” MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said. The remarks came after Pakistan reportedly restricted Taiwanese carriers from using its airspace. Pakistan is the first country reported to have taken such a step against Taiwanese carriers.

Article Title: May instruct courts not to give bail in digital arrest cases: SC
Article Text:
SC said it may restrain courts from granting bail to those arrested for putting senior citizens under digital arrest, calling such crimes "dacoity to say the least".

NEW DELHI: Keeping up the heat on accused in cyber fraud cases, SC on Wednesday said if the situation demands, it will restrain courts from granting bail to those arrested for putting senior citizens under digital arrest to dupe them of their hard-earned life savings.This observation came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana as the counsel for a Delhi-based petitioner, who is accused of providing a mule account for deposit of proceeds of extortion through digital arrest, sought clubbing of numerous cases in different states at one place.Perusing the records, SC said that one of the first victims of this crime syndicate was an 81-year resident of Ernakulam, from whom the criminals allegedly extorted 1.9 crore. “You want such victims of digital arrest and cyber fraud to travel to other states to depose as complainants? The cases will be investigated by police of the state in whose jurisdiction the persons were defrauded through digital arrest,” it noted.“Extortion is a milder term for such crimes. It is dacoity to say the least,” the bench said. When the counsel pleaded that the petitioner had filed a complaint on coming to know of her account being used as a mule account for transfer of ill-gotten monies, the bench said and added, “We will not allow foot soldiers of the crime syndicate to derail investigations. At best, the petitioner can approach the HCs concerned and seek consolidation of investigations into all cases in a state by one agency. ”The apex court bench said the balance of convenience must tilt towards the victims of cyber fraud and digital arrest.The petitioner withdrew her petition.
Article Summary: SC said it may restrain courts from granting bail to those arrested for putting senior citizens under digital arrest, calling such crimes "dacoity to say the least" The apex court bench said the balance of convenience must tilt towards the victims of cyber fraud and digital arrest.

Article Title: SC summons Sanjay Raut in contempt case
Article Text:
File photo: Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Wednesday directed Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut to appear before it in person over a contempt petition for his remarks against CJI Surya Kant and the judiciary. Although journalist Nikhil Wagle is also facing the same charge of scandalising the institution, he has been exempted from physical appearance and asked to be present virtually as he was represented by a lawyer in the court proceedings on Wednesday.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi said that the issue raised is very important as it pertains to the entire institution of the judiciary and sought assistance from lawyers.The contempt petition was filed by Supreme Court Bar Association and all its office-bearers present in court contended that their social media posts were based on fake news and had maligned the judiciary and judges, including CJI.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Raut to appear before it in person. Raut is facing a contempt petition for his remarks against CJI Surya Kant and the judiciary. Journalist Nikhil Wagle is also facing the same charge of scandalising the institution.

Article Title: Ladakh admin rebuts Wangchuk’s claim of liqour shop in every street
Article Text:
File photo: Ladakh administration rejected Sonam Wangchuk's claim of liquor shops opening everywhere, saying only one shop is operational, as he accused it of playing with words over bars.

SRINAGAR: Days after Leh Apex Body member and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk alleged that liquor shops and bars are being opened in every nook and corner of Ladakh, forcing women of the region to protest, the UT administration Wednesday termed his statement as “totally false and misleading” and said only one liquor shop is currently operational in entire Ladakh.In a statement, govt said the excise policy of 2026-27 was notified on June 1. However, upon receiving feedback and suggestions from the people and social organisations, the lieutenant governor rolled back the new policy on Aug 26. The excise policy of 2025-26 was subsequently restored and remains in force, the statement further said.Under the old policy, only two liquor shops were permitted in Leh. While one wine shop became operational after an auction held on Oct 14, no bid was received for the second, the statement mentioned.The statement said 50 liquor retail vends with attached bars and restaurants are currently operational across the UT — 38 in Leh, seven in Nubra, three in Zanskar and two in Changthang. Two beer bars are also operational in Leh. Besides, nine hotels in Leh and one in Nubra hold liquor licences.The licences are issued to applicants in accordance with the “distance criteria” from highways and religious and educational institutions.Hence, Wangchuk’s claim of opening bars “in every street, locality and around school” holds no ground, the statement said.The administration advised Wangchuk to “verify the facts from official sources before feeding completely false and imaginary claims to the national media and the people at large”.Wangchuk responded later in the evening, saying the “LG Ladakh’s administration has finally rolled back its infamous liquor policy after repeated protests from civil society and a week-long sit-in by mother’s groups”. Countering govt’s charges against him, he said: “If it was all lies and rumours, why would 100s (sic.) of mothers leave their children and homes and spend six nights in sub-zero temperatures?”Women’s groups in Ladakh have been protesting for several days, demanding that Ladakh be declared a dry UT. On Tuesday, the administration called for wider consultations to find a middle ground.Wangchuk accused the administration of “playing with words between ‘liquor shop’ & ‘bar’”, and using the celebratory environment during the Dalai Lama’s Ladakh visit to “sneak in many alcohol bars, which reached 50 in number (highest in Ladakh’s history)”.
Article Summary: Sonam Wangchuk alleged that liquor shops and bars are being opened in every nook and corner of Ladakh. But Ladakh administration rejected his claim, saying only one shop is operational. Wangchuk accused the administration of “playing with words between ‘liquor shop’ & ‘bar’”

Article Title: 'India is very strong, watch Dhurandhar': Arunachal minister on ITBP chief's remarks on China border
Article Text:
A file photo of ITBP personnel near Indo-China border. (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India is “very strong” and its intelligence capabilities have grown significantly, Arunachal Pradesh minister Balo Raja said, citing the spy thriller Dhurandhar while questioning ITBP chief Shatrujeet Singh Kapur's reported remarks on continuing face-offs with Chinese forces along the border.Speaking to reporters in Itanagar on Tuesday, Raja, who holds the urban affairs, land management and civil aviation portfolios, questioned why a senior officer would make statements that could create an impression of India being weak."Why make statements like that when you are a DG? Why perceive yourself as weak? India is very strong. You must have seen the 'Dhurandhar' movie; watch it, and you will see how much India's intelligence capabilities have grown," Raja said.His remarks come amid a political controversy over Kapur's reported comments that face-offs at several locations along the frontier in Arunachal Pradesh were continuing.Addressing ITBP personnel at an event in Alwar, Rajasthan, on October 22, Kapur reportedly spoke about the confrontations along the India-China border and praised the force's newly raised Shaurya commando teams for their role in handling them.He also stressed the need to modernise weapons and equipment and strengthen the force's ability to respond to evolving security challenges, including drone warfare.Kapur said traditional methods of warfare were no longer sufficient to counter China, which he described as India's “biggest adversary”.The reported remarks triggered political reactions, with opposition leaders seeking clarity from the Centre on the border situation and the circumstances surrounding the face-offs.The comments came as the ITBP stepped up its modernisation efforts, focusing on emerging warfare technologies, specialised training and improved operational capabilities.Earlier, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) clarified the government's position after reports of Kapur's remarks about continuing face-offs with the People's Liberation Army (PLA) in Arunachal Pradesh.During a briefing on Friday, the MEA said that the situation along the India-China border was occasionally disrupted when Chinese forces deviated from established patrolling patterns."Insofar as the specifics are concerned, I would refer you to the Ministry of Defence. As we have noted in the past, the situation in the India-China border areas gets disturbed from time to time when Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns. Both sides continue to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the Line of Actual Control," the MEA said."The two sides have also agreed to discuss ways to improve understanding of the LAC in appropriate areas for better border management. I would also like to emphasise that the maintenance of peace and tranquillity in the border areas is essential for the overall development of bilateral relations," it added.
Article Summary: Arunachal Pradesh minister Balo Raja cited the spy thriller Dhurandhar while questioning ITBP chief Shatrujeet Singh Kapur's reported remarks on continuing face-offs with Chinese forces along the border. Raja questioned why a senior officer would make statements that could create an impression of India being weak.

Article Title: 22 Indians, including 14 seafarers, killed in West Asia conflict: MEA
Article Text:

(With PTI inputs)

NEW DELHI: India has lost 22 nationals, including 14 seafarers, in the ongoing West Asia conflict, the ministry of external Affairs (MEA) said on Wednesday.According to MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, three Indians had been killed in Saudi Arabia.“We are deeply concerned about the ongoing conflict in West Asia. We have lost 22 Indian nationals in the conflict, including 14 seafarers. We remain in close touch with our community in the Gulf region for their safety and wellbeing. Three Indians have lost their lives in Saudi Arabia,” Jaiswal told reporters at a regular briefing in New Delhi.The war began on February 28, following US and Israeli strikes on Iran. India has consistently called for a resolution through dialogue and diplomacy.Tensions have escalated in recent days after Yemen-based Houthi rebels launched strikes on Saudi Arabia, opening another front in the eight-month-long conflict. Saudi Arabia is also among the Gulf states targeted by Iran for hosting US military bases.India has expressed serious concern over Houthi attacks on the Kingdom’s civilian infrastructure and economic assets, warning that such strikes threaten regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait.The Iran-backed Houthis also attacked Saudi Arabia’s East-West oil pipeline, a key route for crude exports that has become increasingly important since the conflict disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been under a virtual Iranian blockade since March.The Houthi attacks have raised further concerns over the safety of the Bab-el-Mandeb, a strategic maritime chokepoint between the Horn of Africa and the Arabian Peninsula that connects the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea.
Article Summary: India has lost 22 nationals, including 14 seafarers, in the ongoing West Asia conflict. The war began on February 28, following US and Israeli strikes on Iran. According to MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, three Indians had been killed in Saudi Arabia.

Article Title: 'DK, its done bro': BJP's dig at CM Shivakumar after sweeping Karnataka MLC polls
Article Text:
BJP takes a swipe at DK Shivakumar after the NDA wins all four seats in Karnataka Legislative Council elections.

NDA calls victory a sign of things to come

Yediyurappa congratulates winning candidates

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday took a dig at Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar after the BJP-Janata Dal (Secular) alliance won all four seats in the state’s Legislative Council elections for Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies.The Karnataka BJP used the viral phrase “DK, it’s done, bro!” to target the ruling Congress after the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) secured a clean sweep in the polls, winning two Graduates’ seats and two Teachers’ seats.In a post on X, the BJP wrote, “DK, it’s done, bro! NDA SWEEPS 4/4 Teachers’ and Graduates’ constituencies in the MLC elections!”The phrase echoes actor Salman Khan’s widely discussed post, “Sonam, it's done, bro”, during youth and student protests involving the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The remark later became a subject of online satire, memes and political commentary. The BJP has now adapted the line to mock Congress following the alliance’s electoral success.Meanwhile, Shivakumar said the Congress would respectfully accept the people's verdict in the Legislative Council elections for four seats, acknowledging that the party fell short of its expectations and would undertake a detailed review of the results.The elections covered 19 districts, spanning nearly two-thirds of Karnataka, including the home districts of chief minister Siddaramaiah and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge.NDA leaders have presented the result as a sign of support for the alliance among teachers, graduates and educated professionals. They have also described the clean sweep as a preview of the political contest expected in the 2028 Karnataka Assembly elections JD(S) state youth president Nikhil Kumar called the outcome a “historic 4/4 clean sweep” and accused the Congress government of misusing state machinery and power during the election.“A historic 4/4 clean sweep for the NDA in the Karnataka Legislative Council elections (2 Graduate & 2 Teachers' constituencies)!” Kumar wrote on X.He further claimed that voters had rejected the Congress government and said the result reflected the political mood on the ground.“Despite the Congress government misusing state machinery and power, the educated fraternity has rejected their misrule. Spanning 19 districts (nearly 2/3rd of Karnataka), including the home districts of the CM & AICC President Sri @kharge Ji, this ballot paper mandate, free of any EVM debate, reflects the true ground reality!”, he wrote.Kumar also linked the result to the next Assembly election, calling the alliance’s performance a preview of what could lie ahead.“This unified fight by the NDA is a clear trailer for what lies ahead in the 2028 Assembly Elections. A huge thank you to the voters, and my heartiest congratulations to the dynamic leaders and hardworking cadres of both @JanataDal_S and @BJP4Karnataka for this towering victory!”Former Karnataka chief minister BS Yediyurappa also congratulated the four NDA candidates who won the seats, naming Shasheel Namoshi, Dr S V Sankanoor, K M Suresh and A P Ranganath.In a post on X, Yediyurappa described the result as a mandate against the Congress government and an endorsement of the NDA’s politics under Prime Minister Narendra Modi.“My heartiest congratulations to Shri Shasheel Namoshi, Shri Dr. SV Sankanoor, Shri KM Suresh, and Shri A.P. Ranganath, the NDA alliance candidates who have achieved an unprecedented victory in the election to the four seats of the Graduates’ and Teachers’ constituencies in the State Legislative Council.This victory is a clear mandate given by the state’s enlightened voters against the ruling Congress party and an endorsement of the development politics of the NDA government under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji. ”He also thanked voters, party leaders and workers from both the BJP and JD(S) for their efforts during the campaign.“The victorious candidates will work for the people in a manner befitting the trust placed by the voters. Congratulations to all the enlightened voters who reposed faith in and supported our candidates, and to the BJP-JD(S) alliance state presidents, all leaders, people’s representatives, and every dedicated worker who toiled day and night at the field level for this historic victory. My best wishes for the successful tenure of the newly elected legislators,” he added.
Article Summary: BJP takes a swipe at DK Shivakumar after the NDA wins all four seats in Karnataka Legislative Council elections. Karnataka BJP used the viral phrase “DK, it’s done, bro!” to target the ruling Congress. JD(S) state youth president Nikhil Kumar called the outcome a “historic 4/4 clean sweep”

NEW DELHI: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and electric poles, damaging roads and bringing torrential rain, with some areas of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha recording up to 30 cm of rainfall. The storm’s impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for several days of rain, thunderstorms and snowfall from Thursday.The Nepal Meteorological Department’s Weather Forecasting Division said the country was currently experiencing the partial influence of westerly winds, with the approaching cyclone expected to bring widespread precipitation and a risk of heavy rain and snowfall through the weekend.“The country is currently under the partial influence of westerly winds. In addition, the country is expected to come under the influence of Cyclone ‘Arnab’, developed over the Bay of Bengal, from Kartik 12 (Thursday),” the department said in its latest bulletin.Weather conditions remained relatively clear in the Himalayan and hilly regions on Wednesday morning, although fog and mist affected parts of the Terai, valleys and river basins.The department forecast increasing cloud cover and scattered precipitation from Wednesday afternoon, with conditions becoming more unsettled overnight. Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini provinces are among the areas expected to experience rain, while snowfall is possible in Himalayan regions.The risk is forecast to increase on Thursday night, when thunderstorms and lightning could accompany rain and snowfall. Heavy precipitation is possible in parts of Koshi, Bagmati and Gandaki provinces, while some areas of Lumbini could also receive heavy rainfall.Friday and Saturday are expected to bring the most widespread impacts. The department warned that heavy rain or snowfall could affect several provinces, with isolated locations facing the possibility of very heavy precipitation.Its Friday forecast states, “Mostly cloudy throughout the country. Light to moderate rain or snowfall accompanied by thunder and lightning is possible at most places in Koshi, Madhesh, Bagmati, Gandaki and Lumbini Provinces and at many places in Karnali and Sudurpashchim Provinces.”The expected combination of westerly winds and moisture associated with Cyclone Arnab could increase the risk of flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in vulnerable hilly regions. Heavy snowfall could also create hazardous conditions in high-altitude areas.Meanwhile, in India, at least three people died in cyclone Arnab-related incidents in Andhra Pradesh on Wednesday. South Coast Railway (SCoR) cancelled 57 trains and rescheduled 15 others as a precautionary measure. However, officials quoted by ANI said the cyclone had weakened from a very severe to a severe cyclonic storm after moving over land, and was expected to weaken further. Four additional NDRF teams were deployed to Andhra Pradesh.(This is a top Google Trends topic.)
Article Summary: Cyclone ‘Arnab’ has battered India’s eastern coast, uprooting trees and damaging roads. The storm's impact is now expected to extend to Nepal, which is bracing for several days of rain, thunderstorms and snowfall.

Article Title: 'Taking down Instagram accounts won't make questions disappear': Abhijeet Dipke accuses Centre of digital crackdown
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke

NEW DELHI : Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances.On Wednsday, in a post on X, Dipke wrote, “The Instagram crackdown is not going to work!“The government is taking down thousands of posts and accounts every day, but it seems to be missing a fundamental point.“Instagram is just a platform where people are raising their questions. The reasons behind those questions exist far beyond social media, and taking down accounts won't make them disappear,” Dipke wrote, warning that the alleged censorship could further erode trust among the very people the government is supposed to answer to.His remarks come amid wider scrutiny of online content restrictions and freedom of expression. Activists and political groups have raised concerns over account suspensions and takedown directives, including those reportedly issued under Section 69A of the Information Technology Act.According to PTI, social media platforms including Meta and X have been asked by the Centre to restrict posts and handles raising questions on youth unemployment, governance, and public infrastructure.Critics argue that restricting online content does not address underlying concerns over unemployment, examination paper leaks, governance and public infrastructure.The issue has also reached the courts. On October 27, the Delhi High Court issued notice to the Centre and the concerned department on a petition challenging the withholding of the Instagram handle @bring_back__ballot in India.The account is associated with the “Bring Back Ballot” initiative of Mission Save Constitution and advocate Mehmood Pracha, its national convenor.The petition stated that the handle was withheld on October 10, the day organisers held a protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. It displayed the message: “Account not available in India. This is because we complied with a legal request to restrict this content.”The petitioners alleged, “No notice, hearing, reasons or copy of any order was ever furnished to the Petitioners.”The initiative advocated a return to paper ballots under the slogan “EVM Hatao Desh Bachao”. The petition said organisers had informed Delhi Police about the protest on October 9.Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice and sought the Centre’s response. Central Government Standing Counsel Ashish Dixit accepted notice on behalf of the Ministry of Home Affairs, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the designated officer. Advocate Amee Rana accepted notice for Meta Platforms.The matter is listed for hearing on November 6, when the court is expected to consider the petition further.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke criticised the Centre over an alleged crackdown on anti-government posts and accounts on Instagram. He warned that silencing citizens by taking down content would not address the public grievances.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. Article Title: 3 siblings found dead in flat near Mumbai; trio recorded video before tragedy
Article Text:
Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.





VIRAR: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday, with police suspecting they died by suicide after consuming poison.In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties, police said.The deceased were identified as Kumar Mehta (50), Dipesh Mehta (52) and Khevana Mehta (48). They lived in flat No. 1203 in the D wing of Garden Avenue in Global City. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat.Bolinj police reached the spot and broke open the door around 2.30am on Thursday. The bodies were found in a decomposed state inside the flat.According to police, the siblings had been living in the rented flat since 2025. One of them had suffered paralysis, while one of the brothers was undergoing treatment for cancer.In the video recorded in Gujarati before their deaths, they reportedly spoke about their health problems and financial distress.Senior inspector Prakash Kawale of Bolinj police station said the siblings may have died three to four days before their bodies were discovered. Their bodies have been sent for postmortem examination.Police also contacted the siblings’ sister, who told investigators that the three were facing financial difficulties and had sought money from her as well.
Article Summary: Three unmarried siblings were found dead inside their rented flat in the Global City area of Virar (West) on Thursday. Residents alerted police after noticing a strong foul smell coming from the flat. Police suspect they died by suicide after consuming poison. In a video recorded before their deaths, they reportedly cited illness and financial difficulties.

Article Title: Spain train collision that killed 68 sparks protests demanding transport minister’s resignation
Article Text:
Protests following Spain train collision

Spanish trade union CSIF has demanded the resignation of transport minister Óscar Puente following a collision between two high-speed trains that killed at least 68 people and injured around 100, accusing him of shifting responsibility onto a railway official instead of accepting accountability.The crash occurred on Wednesday when a Renfe high-speed train travelling south from Madrid towards Seville collided with a stationary Iryo train. The collision followed a disruption to the railway safety system along a 63-km stretch of track between Madrid and Seville, which automatically stopped trains in the area, Puente said.The state-owned railway infrastructure manager Adif then took manual control of the system and allowed the Renfe train to continue despite a red signal, Puente said. He described the erroneous order as “inexplicable”.CSIF called on the government to respect the investigation and the presumption of innocence of Adif’s head of traffic. It accused Puente of using a railway employee as a scapegoat rather than “assuming his responsibilities”. The union also said it had warned in September about excessive working hours at Adif.The demand for the minister’s resignation came as anger over the crash spilled onto the streets of Madrid on Wednesday night.Around 500 demonstrators gathered outside the Transport Ministry, with some throwing bottles and flares at police, Reuters reported. Police deployed tear gas to disperse the crowd.Protesters called for government officials to resign, holding signs reading “Leave!”, “Criminals” and “Corruption kills”. Prime minister Pedro Sánchez has faced a series of political setbacks and corruption scandals involving close associates this year.Meanwhile, rescue workers continued searching the wreckage under floodlights, with more than 500 emergency personnel deployed to the site. Rail services between Madrid and the Andalusia region remained suspended on Thursday. Prime minister Pedro Sánchez has promised a thorough investigation.

Article Title: Decoys, secret jet and Trump's help: How Bolsonaro pulled off his escape from Brazil to US
Article Text:
After losing Brazil’s election, Flávio Bolsonaro fled to Miami in an elaborate operation aided by Trump’s inner circle and Argentina’s president

Four cars, decoy and a carefully concealed departure

Also Read|

From Argentina to Miami on a private jet

Also Read|

Trump’s approval and a long-running alliance

Flávio Bolsonaro’s journey from Brazil to the United States involved decoy cars, a cross-border transfer through Argentina and Ecuador, and assistance from allies of US President Donald Trump.The defeated Brazilian presidential candidate and his family reached Miami on Wednesday after an operation coordinated by a small circle of US officials and aides to Argentina president Javier Milei, The Wall Street Journal reported.Flávio Bolsonaro’s departure came after he lost Brazil’s presidential runoff election to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Brazil’s Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passports within 24 hours as part of a money-laundering investigation and barred him from leaving the country. Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing.After Bolsonaro stepped off the plane in Miami on Wednesday morning, wearing a navy polo shirt and a backpack, uniformed officers used umbrellas to shield him from cameras.According to the reports, Bolsonaro left his home in Brasília on Monday evening in a convoy of four dark vehicles. The cars split in different directions, leaving journalists and others uncertain about which one was carrying him.The report said that even some of Bolsonaro’s close allies in Washington and Brazil were initially unaware of his whereabouts. By Tuesday afternoon, however, allies were telling reporters that he had reached Florida, although he was still in Brazil at the time.The operation took shape on Monday as people close to Bolsonaro grew concerned that he could face arrest, the WSJ reported. His legal troubles predated the election, but the court order restricting his travel intensified those concerns.Bolsonaro, his wife and their two daughters travelled by road towards Argentina. According to Argentine authorities cited in the report, the family crossed the Tancredo Neves International Bridge into Puerto Iguazú at around 10:50 pm local time on Tuesday.Their vehicle was escorted by Argentine airport security police to the immigration checkpoint at Iguazú Falls International Airport. A former Argentine intelligence official told the newspaper that Santiago Caputo, a senior aide to Milei, was monitoring the operation and coordinating with Bolsonaro’s younger brother, Eduardo Bolsonaro.A private Gulfstream jet, operated by charter airline Baires Fly, was waiting at the airport. Flight-tracking data showed that the aircraft travelled to Guayaquil, Ecuador, to refuel before continuing to the United States.Bolsonaro travelled using an Italian passport. He had reportedly acquired Italian citizenship in 2023.The jet landed at Miami-Opa Locka Executive Airport on Wednesday morning. Officers used umbrellas to shield the family from cameras as they were escorted to a waiting vehicle.The WSJ reported that Trump personally approved the family’s entry into the US on Tuesday, after which secretary of state Marco Rubio moved to issue visas. The family was admitted under humanitarian parole, allowing them to remain in the country for one year, according to people familiar with the arrangements cited by the newspaper.Trump adviser Jason Miller helped secure the charter flight, working with Eduardo Bolsonaro. The operation marked the culmination of years of efforts by the Bolsonaro family to cultivate ties with Trump and his inner circle.In a statement from Miami, Bolsonaro referred to himself as the “leader of Brazil” and thanked Trump for welcoming him to a “land of freedoms”. He also praised Milei for his “courage” and “sense of justice”.Trump, meanwhile, said of the Bolsonaros, “I thought they were treated very unfairly.” He added: “But I won’t get involved—it was a very strange election, that’s for sure.”Bolsonaro is reportedly planning to establish a political operation in exile in the US, although it remains unclear whether the Trump administration will take further steps to intervene in Brazil’s domestic political and legal disputes.
Article Summary: Flávio Bolsonaro fled to Miami after losing Brazil’s presidential runoff election to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Operation involved decoy cars, a cross-border transfer through Argentina and Ecuador, and assistance from allies of US President Donald Trump.

Article Title: Ex-Congress worker shot at, dragged out of car, attacked with sharp weapons in Ludhiana

LUDHIANA: A group of assailants allegedly fired multiple shots at a property dealer and former Congress worker in Dholewal late Wednesday night when he was with his mother and three-year-old son.The victim, Jagjot Singh, sustained a splinter injury near his eye before the attackers allegedly assaulted him with a sharp-edged weapon and fled.Singh, a resident of Miller Gunj, managed to drive away with his mother and son despite the attack and reach Civil Hospital, where he received treatment.Singh said the family had ordered food while sitting in the car. When he stepped out to make a payment and buy a bottle of water, around eight assailants arrived and opened fire at him.He rushed back into the car, but the accused allegedly tried to pull him out and attacked him with sharp-edged weapons. As he resisted and attempted to drive away, they fired several rounds at the car, shattering its windowpanes.Singh alleged that he knew the attackers and claimed the same people had attacked his house and opened fire about a year ago over a rivalry.He also alleged a political angle, saying he was previously associated with the Congress but was no longer affiliated with any political party.He claimed the attackers belonged to another political party and held a grudge against him over electoral rivalry.ACP (Industrial Area-B) Anubhav Jain said police had identified the accused, who allegedly had a rivalry with Singh over their previous political associations. The main accused was identified as Jaswinder Singh, who was accompanied by his aides. An FIR has been registered.
Article Summary: Jagjot Singh, a property dealer and former Congress worker, was with his mother and three-year-old son.
