Article Title: Israel election deadlock: Netanyahu, Eisenkot blocs tied in revised exit polls
Article Text:
File photo: Israel's prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot

Opposition claims mandate for change

Arab parties could prove pivotal

Israel’s latest exit polls show a deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot, with updated projections from public broadcaster Kan and Channel 13 putting both sides at 51 seats each.Channel 12’s revised exit poll gives Netanyahu’s bloc 52 seats and the Eisenkot-led bloc 50, reversing its earlier projection that had the anti-Netanyahu camp marginally ahead.Turnout reached 77.7%, the highest recorded at the close of voting since 1999, according to Israel’s Central Elections Committee. The strong participation came in an election widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership after three years of war and regional conflict.Eisenkot arrived at Yashar party headquarters in Tel Aviv and said, “We made history,” arguing that the public had chosen change and voted against Netanyahu continuing as prime minister. He said it would be a mistake to hold another election given the high turnout and described respecting voters’ wishes as his responsibility.Opposition leader Yair Lapid also declared Netanyahu’s bloc had suffered a defeat. “Don’t let them confuse you: The Netanyahu bloc suffered a harsh defeat,” Lapid wrote on social media, adding that the public had told the government to go home.Netanyahu said it was too early to draw conclusions and that he was waiting for the “real results”. He maintained that Likud was the largest party and called for a “strong right-wing national government”, saying Israel could not be led by a government reliant on “Arab backing”.Kan projected 25 seats for Likud and 21 for Yashar, with the anti-Netanyahu bloc on 53 seats, Netanyahu’s bloc on 50 and Arab-led parties on 17. Channel 13 projected 25 seats for Likud and 23 for Yashar, with 53 seats for the anti-Netanyahu bloc, 50 for Netanyahu’s bloc and 17 for Arab-led parties. Channel 12’s revised projection put Likud on 24 seats and Yashar on 22, with the Jewish-led opposition parties on 52, Netanyahu-supporting parties on 50 and Arab-led parties on 18.The projected 17–18 seats for Arab-led parties could complicate coalition negotiations. Although they oppose Netanyahu, they are outside the main Zionist opposition bloc and have generally not joined governing coalitions. Their position could nevertheless become consequential if neither main bloc can secure enough support to govern.Neither main bloc is projected to reach the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. The result could mean weeks of coalition negotiations and the possibility of another election. Netanyahu would remain caretaker prime minister in the interim, while President Isaac Herzog would consult party leaders and nominate a candidate to try to form a government.Official votes are still being counted, and exit-poll projections may change as further results come in.
Article Summary: Latest exit polls show a deadlock between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ’s bloc and the opposition led by Gadi Eisenkot. Neither main bloc is projected to reach the 61 seats required for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. The result could mean weeks of coalition negotiations and the possibility of another election.

Article Title: 68 killed in Spain train collision: Videos capture overturned carriages, injured passengers, devastation
Article Text:
Aftermath of Spain train collision

At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spain’s central province of Toledo. Videos and photographs from the scene showed overturned carriages, injured passengers and emergency crews working to rescue people trapped in the wreckage.The collision occurred on Wednesday morning near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville rail route. Recordings captured by passengers showed scenes inside the trains following the impact, while images from the site showed carriages lying on their sides beside the tracks.Emergency services rushed to the scene to evacuate passengers, provide medical assistance and search the wreckage for survivors. Injured passengers were taken to nearby medical facilities, including a sports centre converted into a temporary treatment site. The regional government of Castilla-La Mancha said 58 people were receiving treatment in hospitals.According to Spain’s rail infrastructure operator ADIF, both trains were travelling south from Madrid towards Seville when the collision occurred. A state-owned RENFE train struck the rear of an IRYO train that had stopped on the tracks, derailing carriages on both trains.Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente said a failure in the railway’s computer communications system had disrupted safety operations before the collision. The malfunction automatically stopped trains along a 63-kilometre stretch of track, after which the RENFE train was reportedly allowed to proceed despite a red signal.According to accounts of the incident, ADIF took manual control of the system following the failure. Puente said the train was authorised to continue under circumstances that investigators would need to examine.“There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorized to proceed,” Puente said at a press conference on Wednesday. “It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.”The RENFE train reportedly resumed its journey at about 124 miles per hour before hitting the stationary IRYO train. Authorities have yet to establish the full sequence of events leading to the crash.Meanwhile, Spanish trade union CSIF has demanded the resignation of the transport minister following the collision. The union accused Puente of shifting responsibility onto a railway official rather than accepting accountability for the disaster. Anger over the crash spilled onto the streets of Madrid on Wednesday night, when around 500 demonstrators gathered outside the Transport Ministry. Some protesters threw bottles and flares at police, prompting officers to deploy tear gas to disperse the crowd, Reuters reported.The disaster comes after another deadly rail collision in Spain earlier this year. A January crash in Córdoba province killed more than 40 people, while a separate incident near Barcelona claimed the life of a train driver.Rescue teams continued searching the damaged carriages as authorities worked to identify victims, assist survivors and establish the cause of the collision. Investigators are expected to examine the signalling system, communications failure and the decision to allow the train to proceed despite the red signal.
Article Summary: At least 68 people have been killed and dozens injured after a high-speed train collision in Spain’s central province of Toledo. The collision occurred on Wednesday morning near Urda, about 120 km south of Madrid, on the Madrid-Seville rail route.

Article Title: Arab parties claim kingmaker status in Israel
Article Text:
File photo: Yousef Jabareen, leader of Israel's Arab-led Joint List political alliance, (Centre-L) and other members cheer at the alliance's campaign headquarters

Who is Mansour Abbas?

What is Joint List?

How are Arabs placed in Israel

Arab parties' past support

Israel's Arab parties appear to secure a record number of seats in parliament and could emerge as kingmakers after strong turnout in Tuesday's election. Vote tallies show the two main Arab parties on course to win around 19 seats, nearly double their current representation in the Knesset. The two main parties are Yousef Jabareen-led Joint List and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas.Yousef Jabareen, the leader of the Arab-dominated Joint List, said his party would seek to use its projected 12 seats "to facilitate getting rid of Netanyahu's govt and hopefully helping to change the political situation in Israel". Jabareen said the Joint List could not join an Eisenkot-led govt because of its support for Israel's military campaign in Gaza and occupation of southern Lebanon. But he left open the possibility of bolstering Eisenkot's bloc from the outside, propping up a minority govt that could survive confidence votes. "We have our demands to protect our community, to advance the rights of our community and to promote equality for our community," said Jabareen, speaking from his home in the Arab town of Umm al-Fahm.The second main Arab party, Ra'am, is led by Mansour Abbas. He has sought to make Ra'am a more attractive coalition partner, adding a Jewish former police official to its slate and saying he would join an Eisenkot-led govt.Speaking to Israeli television after voting wrapped on Tuesday night, Ra'am chief Mansour Abbas said: "I believe we can overcome the difficulties ... and I think that most voters for the (Eisenkot) bloc do want to see (a) govt with the Ra'am party." He said senior members of Eisenkot's bloc had discussed a possible deal with him even before the election. "Everyone is talking to us, not just the change bloc. A few days ago, a very, very senior member of the right approached me. "Eisenkot ruled out forming a govt with any of the Arab parties during the campaign, citing what he called a lack of shared values, including recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state.Netanyahu's Likud party confirmed it would not negotiate with any Arab party to try to form a govt. "Not a chance," spokesman Guy Levy said at the party's headquarters in Jerusalem. "It's not even a question that should be asked."Mansour Abbas (52) is an Arab-Israeli politician, dentist and leader of Ra'am. Elected to Knesset in 2019, he reshaped Arab politics by advocating a pragmatic, domestic-focused approach. Instead of making engagement conditional on the wider Israeli-Palestinian conflict, he prioritises civil gains for Arab citizens, focusing on crime, socioeconomic inequality, infrastructure and municipal funding. He also briefly served in an Israeli ruling coalition from 2021 to 2022.Joint List is an alliance of Arab-majority parties in Israel, formed in 2015 to unite the vote of Arab citizens. It includes Ahmed Tibi's Ta'al and has historically brought together secular, nationalist and left-leaning parties such as Hadash. It campaigns on civil equality, tackling crime in Arab communities and ending the occupation, and has backed govts from outside rather than joining them.Arab citizens of Israel, who often identify as Arab Israelis or Palestine citizens of Israel, comprise 20% of the population, or roughly 2.1 million people. They are central to the medical sector. Data from Israeli ministry of health and Taub Center for Social Policy Studies in Israel show Arabs account for over 20% of physicians, nearly a quarter of nurses and almost half of licensed pharmacists. Two Arab citizens have served as Supreme Court judges, while Arab engineers, scholars, writers and athletes, have visible public roles.For decades, Arab parties provided outside support to governments. Cabinet representation was limited to individual appointments, including Druze lawmaker Salah Tarif in 2001, Labor's Raleb Majadele in 2007, and later Issawi Frej and Ayoob Kara. A significant change came in 2021 when Abbas's Islamist Ra'am joined Naftali Bennett-Yair Lapid's ruling coalition.
Article Summary: Vote tallies show the two main Arab parties on course to win around 19 seats, nearly double their current representation in the Knesset. The two main parties are Yousef Jabareen-led Joint List and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas.

Article Title: Ghaziabad Murder Case: Sleeping beside daughter, Delhi govt employee stabbed multiple times: How wife, her gym trainer lover plotted attack
Article Text:
Shashank Kanthariya was attacked by his wife Priya's gym trainer, Pratap Singh, while sleeping at home

Affair came to light in September

Wife allegedly left door unlocked

Society guards chased accused

Brother's complaint leads to FIR





GHAZIABAD: Shashank Kanthariya thought his wife was leaving home every morning to go to the gym. But police suspect that the routine became part of a conspiracy to kill him after he discovered her alleged affair with her gym trainer and decided to move out of the city.On Monday morning, while the 35-year-old Delhi government employee was asleep beside his young daughter at their home in Vasundhara, the trainer allegedly entered the house through an unlocked door and stabbed him repeatedly.Kanthariya, a senior accountant with the Delhi government, was taken to a nearby hospital after the attack and is currently admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU). His daughter, who was sleeping beside him, woke up during the assault and began crying, alerting neighbours. The child escaped without injuries.Police arrested Kanthariya's wife, Priya (32), and her suspected lover, Pratap Singh (30), a gym trainer, on Tuesday. Both were produced before a court and sent to judicial custody.According to ACP (Indirapuram) Suryabali Maurya, Singh began working at the gym Priya frequented in Vasundhara in January this year. He became her trainer, and the two allegedly entered into a relationship the following month.The relationship continued until Kanthariya learnt about the alleged affair towards the end of September. He confronted Priya and asked her to end the relationship. He also told her to either change gyms or stop attending the one where Singh worked.Police suspect that the dispute escalated when Kanthariya decided to move out of their home and began looking for a house in Delhi. Priya allegedly opposed the plan, while Kanthariya intended to finalise a property on Sunday.Investigators suspect that Priya informed Singh about her husband's plans and that the two subsequently conspired to kill him.Police said Priya routinely left home around 5am to visit the gym, leaving the front door unlocked while her husband and daughter were asleep. On Monday morning, she allegedly followed the same routine, giving Singh an opportunity to enter the house.Singh allegedly arrived armed with two knives and attacked Kanthariya while he was sleeping. The victim woke up during the assault and raised an alarm, while his daughter began crying. The noise alerted neighbours, who rushed to the house as the attacker fled.ACP Maurya said Singh took advantage of Priya's departure to enter the flat and attack her husband. Police suspect the attack was part of the plan the two had allegedly worked out.After fleeing the house, Singh was spotted by a resident of the society, MT Joshi, who noticed blood on his hands and attempted to catch him. Singh allegedly pushed Joshi aside and continued running, managing to get past the security guards.The guards then chased him on a motorcycle, caught him and handed him over to police. Two knives were recovered from his possession, police said.Meanwhile, neighbours rushed the injured Kanthariya to a nearby hospital. He remains in the ICU, while his daughter was unharmed.Kanthariya's brother, Ritesh, filed a police complaint following the attack. An FIR was subsequently registered against Priya and Singh under sections 109 (attempt to murder), 333 (house trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police arrested both accused on Tuesday and produced them before a court, which remanded them to judicial custody.Kanthariya and Priya married in 2021 and have a young daughter. Police said Priya had been married once before her marriage to Kanthariya.
Article Summary: Shashank Kanthariya was attacked by his wife Priya's gym trainer, Pratap Singh, while sleeping at home in Vasundhara, Delhi. Police suspect the attack was part of a plan the two had allegedly worked out. Priya routinely left home around 5am to visit the gym, leaving the front door unlocked while her husband and daughter were asleep.

Article Title: Dispute between college students in Bhopal escalates at cafe as two seniors threaten junior with knife, pistol
Article Text:
A conflict between senior and junior students at a private college intensified at a cafe (Picture credits: X)





Bhopal: A dispute between senior and junior students of a private college escalated at a cafe in Indrapuri on Tuesday night, with two senior students allegedly threatening their junior with a knife and a pistol. The accused also allegedly pointed the pistol at a Crime Branch constable who intervened to defuse the situation before fleeing the spot. The CCTV footage of the incident went viral on social media platforms.Piplani police registered a case against the two accused under sections related to assault and abuse and launched a search for them. Police said it would be clear whether the pistol was real or fake only after it was recovered.According to police, the complainant, Shivanshu (19), lives in Anand Nagar and is a second-year BPharm student at a private college. The accused, Prithvi and Raj , residents of Nizamuddin Colony, are final-year BTech students at the same college.Police said Prithvi and Raj had allegedly threatened Shivanshu earlier and told him to show them greater respect. The dispute escalated on Oct 16, when Shivanshu and his friends allegedly assaulted Prithvi.A case was registered at Anand Nagar police outpost in connection with that incident.Called for settlement, junior alleges threat:On Tuesday, Prithvi allegedly called Shivanshu to meet him to settle the earlier dispute. Around 9 pm, Shivanshu reached a cafe in Indrapuri with his friends, where Prithvi and Raj were already present.The two seniors allegedly began threatening the group with a knife and a pistol. Crime Branch constable Pankaj Deharia, who was nearby, stepped in to intervene. The accused allegedly pointed the pistol at him as well before fleeing.Piplani police said a case had been registered against both accused and efforts were underway to arrest them. They added that the nature of the pistol would be established after it was recovered.
Article Summary: A dispute between senior and junior students escalated at a cafe in Indrapuri. Two senior students allegedly threatened their junior with a knife and a pistol. The accused also allegedly pointed the pistol at a Crime Branch constable who intervened to defuse the situation before fleeing the spot. CCTV footage of the incident went viral on social media platforms.

Article Title: 'Masked people' vandalise Jamia campus, gate brought down, CCTV control room damaged
Article Text:
The university said footage and social media posts indicated the use of iron rods, hammers and other tools. (Photo credit: X)





NEW DELHI: Jamia Millia Islamia witnessed widespread vandalism late Tuesday night, with masked unidentified people allegedly damaging university gates and boundary walls, prompting the administration to express serious concerns over campus security.In a statement Wednesday, the university said its proctorial team and teachers rushed to the campus after receiving reports of attacks.They found that some individuals had brought down Gate No. 4C, pelted stones and damaged the CCTV control room, cameras and their connections. The university also alleged that masked individuals reached the boys’ hostels to mobilise support.According to the administration, the vandalism began shortly after its seventh attempt at dialogue with protesters Tuesday evening. It alleged women faculty members, wardens and provosts were threatened when they tried to reason with female protesters.The university said footage and social media posts indicated the use of iron rods, hammers and other tools.Security remained tight Wednesday, with the campus wearing a deserted look amid prohibitory orders under BNSS Section 163. Police also detained some students outside the campus.The university has extended the period for online classes till Nov 24, stating the situation is not conducive for academic environment.Exams scheduled for Dec will also be held online.Meanwhile, the hunger strike over restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union entered its 17th day. Five students are fasting. Ebin Basil, who began on Oct 12, has lost 7.1 kg, while Rehan Khan, on his 14th day, has lost 4 kg.Three others joined Monday. Doctors have appealed to the vice-chancellor and expressed concern over Ebin and Rehan’s deteriorating health.The deadlock persists despite the university’s Oct 26 order agreeing to hold elections 15 days after approval of the union constitution, revoke suspensions and show-cause notices, and institute an inquiry into security staff conduct.Students want the constitution approved by Dec 20, followed by elections within 15 days.A university spokesperson told TOI the administration had no objection in principle to a students’ union but needed time to examine documents, including previous incidents of violence, court orders and Lyngdoh Committee recommendations.The university also cited the need to prepare a voter list of about 24,000 students.Meanwhile, amid the ongoing agitation, the university’s Foundation Day celebrations scheduled for Thursday have been cancelled for the first time.Several hostel residents were seen leaving Wednesday, amid allegations that students had been asked to vacate hostels following the shift to online classes.
Article Summary: Jamia Millia Islamia witnessed widespread vandalism late Tuesday night, with masked unidentified people allegedly damaging university gates and boundary walls. The university said footage and social media posts indicated the use of iron rods, hammers and other tools. Security remained tight Wednesday, with the campus wearing a deserted look amid prohibitory orders.

Article Title: Uber cabbie arrested for physically restraining, threatening Gurgaon techie over fare dispute; how ordeal unfolded
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





GURGAON: The Uber driver, who allegedly threatened a woman, physically restrained her and followed her to her home over a fare dispute, was arrested on Wednesday after police took suo motu cognizance of her social media post.“Teams from Palam Vihar police station and the Sector 39 crime branch used technical assistance to identify the accused — Yasir (26) from Nuh’s Ghasera village — and gather information about him before arresting him,” police spokesperson Sandeep Turan said. TOIhad reported the incident on Wednesday.Police said preliminary investigation revealed that Yasir had created his Uber account using the name Jamil Jahid Khan, the name mentioned by the woman in her post on X. The woman, a software engineer and artificial intelligence professional, had posted that the driver demanded Rs 1,479 against the fare of around Rs 625 displayed on her Uber app for a ride from Delhi airport to the city. She alleged that when she refused to pay the higher amount, the driver misbehaved with her and threatened to kill her. The incident sparked concern on social media, with users urging the police to take action and calling for stronger measures to protect passengers.According to the police, the matter came to their notice during social media monitoring. Police attempted to contact the woman through X before taking suo motu cognizance and registering an FIR on the basis of her post. In her account of the incident, the woman said the confrontation took place around 4.45am after she booked the Uber cab from Delhi airport for what she described as a 20-minute ride.The app showed a fare of approximately Rs 625, but the driver allegedly demanded Rs 1,479 after showing her a screenshot of a fare quote from Rapido.She said she paid the fare displayed on the Uber app, following which the driver allegedly locked the car and refused to let her retrieve her luggage unless she paid the higher amount. She alleged that he held her arm, followed her to her residence, forced the gate and threatened her life. The woman also raised concerns over her inability to access Uber’s safety support option while trying to report the incident. She later said Uber had contacted her and confirmed that the driver had been barred from the platform.“We were committed to ensuring women’s safety and that strict legal action would be taken against anyone found involved in acts that threaten or compromise women’s safety,” Turan added.The provisions, under which the accused has been arrested, relate to assault or use of criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty (Section 74), words, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman (Section 79), punishment for wrongful restraint (Section 126(2)), wrongful confinement (Section 127), punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation (Section 131), criminal intimidation (Section 351(2)) and the right of private defence of body and property (Section 35) of BNS.
Article Summary: Uber driver allegedly threatened a woman, physically restrained her and followed her to her home over a fare dispute. The woman, a software engineer and artificial intelligence professional, had posted that the driver demanded Rs 1,479 against the fare of around Rs 625 displayed on her Uber app. The incident sparked concern on social media.

Article Title: Delhi man stabbed to death for asking 'extra choley'
Article Text:
(AI-IMAGE) A deadly altercation erupted in Nihal Vihar, Delhi, leaving 35-year-old Sandeep fatally stabbed over extra choley





NEW DELHI: A 35-year-old car driver, who was stabbed multiple times following an alleged dispute over asking for "extra choley" in outer Delhi's Nihal Vihar area, died during treatment on Tuesday, according to news agency PTI.The victim, identified as Sandeep, was allegedly attacked during a scuffle with a choley-bhaturey seller near Jwalapuri Nala on Sunday.The accused, identified as Chintu Gupta, has been arrested and remanded to judicial custody. Police said a murder charge was added to the case following Sandeep's death.Sandeep was initially admitted to Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital on the night of October 25 before being shifted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital in Punjabi Bagh, where he died during treatment on Tuesday.According to his medico-legal case (MLC) report, Sandeep had three stab wounds on the left side of his abdomen, three lacerated wounds on his left forearm and another lacerated wound on his wrist.A senior police officer said Sandeep was declared unfit to give a statement, following which investigators began examining the circumstances of the incident. The preliminary inquiry revealed that a scuffle had taken place between him and the food vendor near Jwalapuri Nala, the officer said.An FIR was registered at Paschim Vihar West police station on Sunday under Section 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), which deals with attempt to murder. Police said the provision was invoked after considering the nature of the injuries and the circumstances of the incident.During the investigation, Gupta was arrested and remanded to judicial custody. Following Sandeep's death, police added Section 103(1) of the BNS, which deals with murder, to the case.Sandeep's father, Bijender Singh, alleged that a minor disagreement over food had escalated into a violent confrontation. He said his son had gone to a Sunday market and asked the vendor for extra choley. An argument followed, during which the vendor allegedly abused Sandeep. The dispute then escalated into a scuffle, and Sandeep was stabbed repeatedly, Singh alleged."I got to know about the incident and immediately reached the spot. Some eyewitnesses also helped me pick him up," Sandeep's father said.Singh said his son was initially taken to a nearby hospital, but he later arranged for him to be shifted to another facility for better treatment. Sandeep was eventually admitted to Maharaja Agrasen Hospital in Punjabi Bagh, where he died on Tuesday, two days after the alleged attack."My son's only fault was that he asked the shopkeeper for some extra choley. He was stabbed several times and died after battling for his life for two days," Singh alleged.Sandeep, a resident of Rav Vihar in Nihal Vihar, worked as a private car driver. He is survived by his wife and two sons, aged four and 10.Singh further alleged that three to four people were involved in the attack, but police had arrested only the vendor so far. "We want justice. All those involved in the killing should be identified and arrested," Singh added.Police said further investigation was underway and they were examining the role of other people allegedly involved in the attack.
Article Summary: Car driver Sandeep, 35, allegedly attacked during scuffle with choley-bhaturey seller. Alleged incident took place in outer Delhi's Nihal Vihar area on Sunday. Police said a murder charge was added to the case following Sandeeping's death.

Article Title: Judge named accused in son’s fatal Mercedes crash gets interim protection from arrest
Article Text:
Jayabalakrishnan, who ran a roadside eatery, was heading home after closing the shop when the accident occurred at 2.20 am on Sunday. Both vehicles were travelling towards Kalamassery.





KOCHI: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge whose 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider.Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal in Irinjalakuda, Thrissur district.“The police shall not arrest the applicant until further orders. However, he shall appear before the investigating officer today at 1pm and if necessary as and when called for. The interrogation of the applicant shall be done in accordance with the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court,” the court ordered.Senior advocate P Vijaya Bhanu, appearing for the judge, told the court that his client had appeared before the police on Wednesday and was interrogated for more than four hours. Another notice directing him to appear before the police had since been issued.According to Bar and Bench, questioning the need for further interrogation and custodial questioning, the court remarked, “What was the need to interrogate him for four hours and now for further interrogation? Why is his arrest required? He is a judicial officer.He will co-operate with the investigation.”Counsel representing the victim’s legal heirs opposed the plea, alleging that the judge had tampered with evidence after being informed of the accident.The court said it had to proceed strictly in accordance with the law and granted interim protection from arrest. It also asked the prosecutor to provide the state’s response to the plea.The judge was named as an accused in the FIR registered after the October 25 crash in Cheranalloor, Kochi, in which his minor son allegedly drove the car that hit a two-wheeler, killing Jayabalakrishnan.In his anticipatory bail plea, the judge claimed he had no knowledge that the vehicle had been taken from the premises. He said he learnt of the accident after receiving a phone call while asleep.The plea also argued that Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which deals with culpable homicide not amounting to murder, requires knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.Meanwhile, the victim’s family has complained to the Kerala high court chief justice seeking an inquiry into the judicial officer’s conduct. According to Bar & Bench, the High Court’s Administrative Committee held a preliminary meeting on October 27 and decided to await further material from the investigating agency before taking any action against the judge.
Article Summary: The Kerala high court on Thursday granted interim protection from arrest to the additional district judge. His 17-year-old son allegedly drove a Mercedes-Benz that hit a two-wheeler in Kochi, killing the rider. Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on an anticipatory bail plea filed by the judge, who is posted at a Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.

Article Title: TVK leader Christopher arrested for sexually harassing college student after offering lift
Article Text:
TVK leader Christopher





KANYAKUMARI: A functionary of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Thursday for allegedly sexually harassing a college student after offering her a lift home in Tamil Nadu’s Kanyakumari district, police said.Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him. He hails from Marundhukottai near Thuckalay.The complainant, a second-year college student from Kulasekaram, studies at a private college in Nagercoil. She regularly travelled with another student from Moolachal, who is also a TVK member, police sources said.On the day of the incident, the two students were waiting for a bus after college when it began raining. Christopher, who knew the other student, stopped his car and offered to drop them home, saying he was travelling in the same direction.After dropping the other student at Moolachal, Christopher continued towards Kulasekaram with the complainant, assuring her that he would drop her near her home, police said.The student alleged that Christopher stopped the vehicle along the way and sexually harassed her. She confronted him and tried to get out of the car to escape, according to police sources. He later dropped her near her residence and fled.The student informed her parents after reaching home and subsequently told her college friend about the incident. The two then approached Thuckalay police station and lodged a complaint.Further investigation is under way.
Article Summary: Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) functionary arrested for allegedly sexually harassing a college student. Christopher, a member of the party’s central district executive committee, had been absconding since a case was registered against him.

Article Title: 6 dead in MP: 2 sisters, one 8 months pregnant, and 4 children found in separate wells
Article Text:
Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday.





BHOPAL: Two sisters, one of whom was eight months pregnant, allegedly jumped into wells with their four children in two separate incidents in Madhya Pradesh’s Shivpuri district on Wednesday, leaving all six dead.Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, Sita Rawat, 40, was found dead with her three children — Rakhi, 14, Priyanka, 11, and Shlok, 6 — in a well in Khonkar village, under Kolaras police station limits.Police are investigating the two incidents separately and are yet to establish the reasons behind the deaths.Anjali’s three daughters were also present when she allegedly jumped into the well with her son. Her eldest daughter, Monika, rescued herself and her two younger sisters before returning home and informing family members. Relatives rushed to the spot and pulled Anjali and Prashant out of the well, but both had died. Anjali’s unborn child also died.According to family members, Anjali’s husband, Dharmveer Singh Rawat, died in a road accident around one-and-a-half months ago.Police are examining the circumstances surrounding the incident.Sita, a resident of Sesai village, had gone to a field in Khonkar village with her three children. When they had not returned home by around 6pm, relatives began searching for them.They found slippers near a well and spotted a child’s body inside, following which they alerted the police. Kolaras police retrieved the bodies of Sita and her three children by around 11pm.Family members said the sisters were close and frequently spoke to each other over the phone. They suspect Sita may have been affected by Anjali’s death earlier that day, but police have not established any link between the two incidents.Postmortem examinations of all six deceased were scheduled for Thursday. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding both incidents.
Article Summary: Two sisters from Madhya Pradesh committed suicide by jumping into wells with their children on Wednesday. Anjali Rawat, 35, allegedly jumped into a well with her six-year-old son, Prashant, in Gungargaon village, under Bairad police station limits, around 1pm. Hours later, her elder sister, SitaRawat, 40, was found dead with her three children in a well in Khonkar village. Police are investigating the two incidents separately.

A deadly shooting occurred at Hotel Bilas Inn in Guwahati, leaving five people dead and one injured.

Accused arrested, licensed pistol seized

Congress raises law and order concerns

GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Police apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting.A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. His condition was stable, a senior doctor said.A forensic and scientific investigation is underway, with specialised teams examining the crime scene and collecting evidence. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Assam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. He called on chief minister and home minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to take responsibility and pay greater attention to rising crime.Gogoi, the deputy leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, also called for a thorough inquiry, accountability and concrete measures to prevent similar incidents.
Article Summary: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night. The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker. The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, was arrested within an hour of the incident.

Article Title: Son of AAP sarpanch shot dead in Amritsar after offering prayers at gurdwara, friend injured; police hunt for 4 accused

Teerath Singh (L) was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village while his friend sustained injuries (R: File photo used for representation)

AMRITSAR: The son of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) sarpanch was shot dead and his friend was injured when assailants opened fire on them outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village, falling under Chatiwind police station, on Monday evening.The victim, Teerath Singh, was returning after paying obeisance at the gurdwara along with his friend Ranjit Singh when the assailants allegedly opened indiscriminate fire, leaving both injured.Teerath was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead, officials said.Yadwinder Singh, Deputy superintendent of police (DSP), Attari, said that Ranjit, who sustained a bullet injury, is undergoing treatment and is stated to be out of danger.The preliminary investigations suggested that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.He further said police have identified four persons, Gurditt Singh, Gurjant Singh, Harkirat Singh alias Hockey, and Gora, and registered an FIR naming them, but no arrests have been made so far.The DSP said that teams have been constituted to investigate the case and arrest the accused.Police sources also informed that the family of Teerath also suspects the involvement of a rival group from the village behind the incident.Notably, Teerath’s brother Karaj Singh had won the sarpanch election on an AAP ticket.The killing triggered a political attack on the AAP government, with former union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu questioning its ability to maintain law and order in Punjab.In a X post, he said, “The murder of Teerath Singh, brother of an incumbent AAP sarpanch, outside a gurdwara in Amritsar is a stark indictment of Punjab’s collapsed law and order. Not a single day passes without the state being shaken by gunfire. When even the ruling party’s own representatives and their families are not safe, the security of ordinary citizens is left in God’s hands. Bhagwant Mann must be held accountable for this spiralling violence. ""Either enforce the writ of the state and ensure people’s safety, or resign. Punjab cannot be expected to keep picking up bodies day after day,” the post read further.
Article Summary: Teerath Singh was shot dead outside a gurdwara in Cheete Kalan village. His friend Ranjit Singh sustained a bullet injury. Preliminary investigations suggest that the murder stemmed from an old animosity over a land dispute, the DSP said while ruling out any political rivalry.

Article Title: Cyclone Arnab disrupts Howrah-Chennai route in Odisha; 9 trains cancelled, 14 diverted after Bahuda river crosses danger mark at 2 bridges
Article Text:
Cyclone Arnab caused significant disruption to rail services along the Howrah-Chennai route in Odisha (Representative image)





BHUBANESWAR: Cyclone Arnab disrupted rail services on the Howrah-Chennai route on Thursday, with nine trains cancelled and 14 others diverted after the swollen Bahuda river crossed the danger mark at two railway bridges in Odisha's Ganjam district, officials said.The East Coast Railway said the Vande Bharat Express connecting Bhubaneswar with Visakhapatnam, the Bhubaneswar-Visakhapatnam Intercity Express, and the Visakha Express, which runs between Bhubaneswar and Secunderabad in Telangana, were among the major trains cancelled, news agency PTI reported.Train services in the Ichchapuram-Jhadupudi section of the Visakhapatnam Division were affected because water was flowing above the danger level at two bridges on the route, it said."Nine trains have been cancelled, and 14 others diverted to ensure passenger safety. Railway officials are closely monitoring the situation. Train services will be restored once the water level recedes and the section is declared safe for train operations," an official said.In another statement, the East Coast Railway said 550mm of rain brought by Cyclone Arnab in Ganjam district had led to a sharp rise in the water level of the Bahuda river, PTI reported.The water level at Baghalati Dam on the Bahuda River crossed the danger mark following heavy rainfall. This led to a rise in water levels at railway bridges between Ichchapuram and Jhadupudi, it said.Officials said several precautionary measures had been taken to ensure passenger safety, with several trains on the Howrah-Chennai route diverted.With passengers stranded at different locations, the railways have made arrangements to provide them with food and water, PTI reported.Additional manpower has been deployed to guide passengers, address their grievances and provide necessary assistance, it said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Cyclone Arnab caused significant disruption to rail services along the Howrah- Chennai route in Odisha. Nine trains were cancelled and 14 others diverted after the swollen Bahuda river crossed the danger mark at two railway bridges in Ganjam district. Train services will be restored once the water level recedes and the section is declared safe for train operations.

Article Title: Magnitude 5.1 earthquake reported in Andaman and Nicobar Islands
Article Text:
An earthquake measuring 5.1 in magnitude struck 218 km north-northwest of Bamboo Flat in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands





PORT BLAIR: A magnitude 5.1 earthquake was reported 218km north-northwest (NNW) of Bambooflat in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, according to the initial information provided.Further details, including the time of the earthquake , its depth, and whether the tremors were felt by residents, were not available in the information provided.There was also no immediate information on damage or casualties.Earthquakes have been recorded in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in recent months. A magnitude 4.6 earthquake struck the islands on February 2, 2026, at around 3.30am, according to the National Centre for Seismology (NCS).(With PTI inputs)

Article Title: Bangladesh: Hindu salon owner stabbed to death over unpaid haircut bills; one arrested
Article Text: Days after a Hindu schoolteacher was beaten to death in a land dispute, another Hindu man has been killed in Bangladesh. A 43-year-old salon owner was allegedly stabbed to death following a dispute over payment for haircuts in Mymensingh district. Police have arrested a 28-year-old man in connection with the killing.According to Bangladeshi media outlet Prothom Alo, at least 10 stab wounds were found on Rishi’s throat, larynx, chest, back and hands. The incident occurred in the Jamirdia area of Bhaluka upazila on Tuesday evening, according to local media reports.The deceased, identified as Rabindra Rishi, owned Apurba Hair Cutting salon at Muktijoddha Market in Bhaluka. Prothom Alo reported that the accused, Saddam Hossain, allegedly attacked Rishi with a sharp weapon after a dispute over unpaid bills and his refusal to provide haircuts on credit.Rishi’s wife, Suchitra Rani Rishi, told local media that Hossain frequently took money from her husband for drugs and did not pay for haircuts. She said the two had argued over the unpaid amounts and that Hossain had threatened to kill her husband a few days before the incident.According to the murder complaint filed by Rishi’s mother, Sulak Rani Rishi, at Bhaluka Model Police Station, the attack took place at around 5.30 pm (local time). Rishi was sitting inside his salon and talking to his brother, Manik Rishi, when Hossain allegedly entered with a sharp knife and stabbed him repeatedly in the neck.The complaint states that Rishi attempted to escape to a nearby shop, where he was stabbed in the chest. He then sought refuge in the courtyard of a nearby house, where the accused allegedly knocked him to the ground and stabbed him in the chest, back and hand. Rishi died from his injuries.Police arrested Hossain and produced him before a court, which sent him to jail. The court scheduled November 1 for a hearing on the police request for five days of remand to question the accused. The investigation is ongoing.The killing comes days after another Hindu man, 55-year-old schoolteacher Manoranjan Roy, was reportedly beaten to death during an arbitration meeting over a land dispute in Dinajpur district. Police said Roy had attempted to mediate between the parties and calm tensions before he was killed.
Article Summary: Rabindra Rishi, 43, was allegedly stabbed to death in Mymensingh district. Police have arrested a 28-year-old man in connection with the killing. Rishi's wife told local media that the two had argued over the unpaid amounts.

Visitors bore stamps on their wrists, which the students transferred onto their own wrists in the May heat. Jail authorities failed to notice that three times as many visitors left as had enteredThirteen prisoners escaped by digging a tunnel near the prison's wallThe first person to make an unauthorised exit from Tihar was an American smuggler, Daniel WalcottSunil Kumar Gupta, former spokesperson and legal advisor to Tihar Jail, offered insights into the reasons behind several prison escapes:Gupta explained that, in one case, inmates wanted to meet their families. In the 2015 escape, the two inmates reportedly wanted to break free from the restrictions of prison life and live without its rules and constraintsIn his book, Gupta also discusses two other prison escapes, one in 1981 and another in 2004. In the 1981 incident, an inmate escaped on the pretext of receiving medical treatment. In the 2004 incident, an escaped inmate reportedly asked a jail official for directions to a bus stop while outside the prisonMore than 5,000 personnel, including prison staff and external security forces, are deployed across Delhi’s three prison complexesSecurity is organised into four layers: prison staff in the first, Tamil Nadu Special Police (TSP) in the second, Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in the third and Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) in the fourthTihar Jail staff manage internal prison operations; TSP personnel guard watchtowers and high-security areas; ITBP personnel handle day-to-day patrolling; and CRPF personnel guard the gatesMore than 7,000 cameras are installed across the three prison complexes, with dedicated rooms for monitoring the footageRoutine inspections and day-to-day security assessments are conducted to identify and address potential vulnerabilitiesTihar and Mandoli prison complexes have large-scale mobile signal jammers, while Rohini Jail also has jamming systems to restrict unauthorised mobile phone usePrison authorities conduct thorough cell searches and unannounced checks to detect prohibited items and prevent security breachesDelhi Armed Police personnel escort inmates when they are taken outside prison premisesInmates are not permitted to clean sewers. Instead, the relevant agency is called in to carry out the work. Its personnel are subject to security checks and are required to enter and exit through a designated gatePrison staff are periodically transferred to prevent them from developing overly close relationships with inmates and to reduce the risk of collusionThe deployment at Tihar began in Aug 1980, following security concerns raised by the 1976 jailbreak. The rationale was to bring in personnel from another state to reduce the risk of local connections and potential collusion between prisoners and prison staff
Article Summary: 17 undertrials escaped from Thekkam patti prison in Tamil Nadu's Theni district this week. Delhi's three prisons can house over 20K inmates. More than 5,000 personnel, including prison staff and external security forces, are deployed across Delhi’s three prison complexes.

Article Title: Judge suspended by HC over alleged misconduct
Article Text:
TOI





New Delhi: Delhi High Court has suspended a district judge with immediate effect, pending disciplinary proceedings. District judge, south, Mohinder Virat, is suspended as a disciplinary proceeding is contemplated against him, the HC administration said in an order issued Tuesday.“It is further ordered that during the period that this order shall remain in force, the headquarters of Mohinder Virat shall be the office of principal district & sessions judge, south, Saket,” the order says, adding that Virat shall not leave Delhi without obtaining permission of the competent authority.reached out to HC registrar general Reetesh Singh several times for comments, but there was no response.However, sources confirmed that the action had been taken over a recent incident involving the judge at a public place, of which there might also be CCTV footage. After the details were conveyed to the higher authorities, a decision to suspend the judicial officer was taken, they said.Virat was till last year on deputation to Delhi govt, where he served as special secretary, law, justice and legislative affairs. Prior to that, he also served as legal adviser at New Delhi Municipal Council in 2023.He was appointed district judge, south, Saket, in Aug this year.He joined Delhi Judicial Service on March 6, 2003, and began his career as a civil judge at Karkardooma in Aug 2003, serving in the position until July 2007. In 2010, he was appointed full-time secretary of District Legal Services Authority, south west, on deputation. He later served in Patiala House and Rohini courts and was promoted to Delhi Higher Judicial Service in Jan 2014.The latest suspension comes months after the high court suspended two judicial officers in quick succession after finding prima facie evidence of misconduct against them earlier this year.In July, the high court administration had suspended judge Veena Rani and fellow judge Vinay Singhal following a full court meeting.Singhal was suspended after a vigilance probe led the then Chief Justice to act against allegations of misconduct in the process of appointing court auctioneers.
Article Summary: District judge, south, Mohinder Virat, is suspended as a disciplinary proceeding is contemplated against him. Virat was till last year on deputation to Delhi govt, where he served as special secretary, law, justice and legislative affairs.

Article Title: Wife leaves at 5.17am, lover enters 3 minutes later: CCTV captures plot to kill Ghaziabad man; victim survives
Article Text:
In photo: The couple and video the gym trainer Pratap entering the house

CCTV footage shows Priya leaving her house and heading towards her car

The gym trainer Pratap entering the house

Neighbours chase trainer after alleged attack

CCTV footage of resident who was out for a morning walk chased Pratap

Pratap runs through the society gate

Neighbours gathered outside the house

An 'affair'

Police suspect dispute over plan to move out

Wife left door unlocked for trainer

Both arrested





GHAZIABAD: CCTV footage has emerged showing the sequence of events in which a woman and her gym trainer allegedly plotted an attack on her husband, who was stabbed while sleeping beside their young daughter in Ghaziabad on Monday.The footage, recorded on October 26, shows Priya leaving her house around 5.17am and driving away in her car.About three minutes later, at 5.20am, her alleged lover, Pratap Singh, a gym trainer, is seen entering the house. Singh allegedly attacked Shashank Kanthariya, 35, while he was asleep beside his daughter. He is seen leaving the house at around 5.23am.At around 5.25am, another neighbour is seen looking through a window and calling out to Shashank.A local resident who was out for a morning walk noticed Singh and, along with a security guard, chased him. Other residents also joined the chase.According to neighbours, Singh told them that nothing had happened. With the help of two men on motorcycles and a security guard, he was eventually caught near the society’s main gate.With the help of two men on motorcycles and a security guard, he was eventually caught near the society’s main gate.By 5.42am, several neighbours and local residents had gathered near his house.Shashank, a senior accountant with the Delhi government, was rushed to a nearby hospital after the attack. He remains in the intensive care unit (ICU). His daughter, who woke up during the assault and began crying, escaped without injuries.According to ACP (Indirapuram) Suryabali Maurya, Singh began working at the gym Priya attended in Vasundhara in January this year. The two allegedly entered into a relationship the following month.Police said Shashank learnt about the alleged affair towards the end of September and confronted his wife, asking her to end the relationship. He also told her to change gyms or stop attending the one where Singh worked.Investigators suspect that tensions escalated after Shashank decided to move out of their home and began looking for a house in Delhi. He reportedly intended to finalise a property on Sunday, while Priya allegedly opposed the move.Police suspect Priya informed Singh about her husband’s plans and that the two conspired to kill him.Police said Priya routinely left home around 5am to go to the gym, leaving the front door unlocked while her husband and daughter were asleep. Investigators suspect she followed the same routine on Monday, allowing Singh to enter the house.Singh allegedly carried two knives and attacked Shashank before fleeing. A resident, identified as M T Joshi, reportedly noticed blood on Singh’s hands and tried to catch him. Singh allegedly pushed him aside and continued running before security guards and residents chased and caught him. Police said two knives were recovered from his possession.Shashank’s brother, Ritesh, filed a complaint following the attack. Police registered a case against Priya and Singh under sections 109 (attempt to murder), 333 (house trespass after preparation for hurt, assault or wrongful restraint) and 61(2) (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Both accused were arrested on Tuesday, produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody.Shashank and Priya married in 2021 and have a young daughter. Police said Priya had been married once before her marriage to Shashank.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows Priya leaving her house around 5.17am and driving away in her car. Three minutes later, at 5.20am, her alleged lover, Pratap Singh, is seen entering the house. Singh allegedly attacked Shashank Kanthariya, 35, while he was asleep beside his daughter.

Article Title: Fire at South Carolina nuclear site triggers emergency; restrictions lifted after no contamination detected
Article Text:
Savannah River National Laboratory in US' South Carolina

A fire at the Savannah River National Laboratory in US' South Carolina triggered a site-area emergency on Wednesday, disrupting road, rail and air movement around the nuclear facility. Traffic restrictions have since been lifted after the fire was extinguished and officials confirmed that radiological surveys detected no contamination outside the site.The emergency was terminated at 9:45 pm local time on Thursday, following which site barricades were reopened and protective measures lifted, according to the SRS. Employees were asked to report for their shifts as usual.“A fire was reported at the Savannah River National Laboratory but has since been extinguished. Radiological surveys indicated no detectable levels of contamination. Highway 125 remains open at this time. SRS officials are directing response efforts and have notified the appropriate state and local government agencies,” the site said in a statement.The fire triggered restrictions on incoming traffic and affected air and rail movement in the surrounding area. Officials declared a “Site Area Emergency”, the second-highest of three emergency categories at the facility, indicating that a significant incident had occurred.The Savannah River Site is a major US government installation that once produced materials used in nuclear weapons, primarily tritium and plutonium-239. Opened in the early 1950s during the Cold War, the complex now focuses on environmental cleanup, nuclear waste management and the handling of nuclear materials, according to the US Department of Energy.The laboratory, located in the north-western part of the site, conducts experiments involving nuclear materials and processes radioactive substances. It also operates a facility that recovers radioisotopes from used nuclear fuel.Edwin Lyman, director of nuclear power safety at the Union of Concerned Scientists, said the confirmation of no contamination beyond the site was reassuring. However, he stressed the need for caution when fires occur in facilities handling radioactive materials.“If you have a fire where there is radioactive material, you need to take extreme precautions because of the potential dispersal of that material and the potential for contamination, potential for the public to be exposed,” Lyman said.While officials have confirmed that the fire is out and no detectable off-site contamination was found, the incident has renewed attention on emergency preparedness at facilities handling radioactive materials.
Article Summary: A fire at the Savannah River National Laboratory in US' South Carolina triggered a site-area emergency on Wednesday. Traffic restrictions have since been lifted after the fire was extinguished and officials confirmed that radiological surveys detected no contamination outside the site. The emergency was terminated at 9:45 pm local time on Thursday.
